questions.stem: When is the greatest opportunity to eliminate a lifecycle hazard at the lowest redesign cost?
options: After commissioning and full production
Only after the first recordable injury
At final decommissioning
During concept and early design stages
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Early decisions determine materials, layout, access, energy, and process choices before change becomes difficult and expensive.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Late changes are often constrained by installed equipment and sunk costs.
Waiting for harm defeats the preventive purpose of design review.
Decommissioning controls end-of-life risk but is too late for operational design hazards.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 35, PtD assessment stages, pp. 780-788

questions.stem: A new tank requires frequent internal cleaning. Which design most strongly applies PtD?
options: Provide clean-in-place capability and external access so routine entry is unnecessary
Add a larger confined-space warning sign
Buy additional retrieval tripods
Schedule entry only on weekends
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Designing the maintenance function to occur without entry eliminates the exposure rather than managing repeated entry.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A warning communicates the hazard but preserves the entry requirement.
Rescue equipment is important but does not eliminate routine entry.
Scheduling does not change the confined-space hazard.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 35, hierarchy of controls and lifecycle design reviews, pp. 783-791

questions.stem: A process can use either a large inventory of concentrated corrosive or a smaller on-demand dilute stream. Which choice is more inherently safer?
options: Store the larger inventory and add more PPE
Generate and use the smaller dilute quantity on demand
Keep the concentrated inventory but increase warning signs
Use the larger inventory and rely on emergency response
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Minimization and moderation reduce the quantity and severity of hazardous material present in the process.
incorrectOptionExplanations: PPE does not reduce the stored hazard magnitude.
Warnings do not reduce inventory, concentration, or release potential.
Emergency response mitigates consequences after loss of control rather than minimizing the hazard.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 35, risk avoidance, elimination, substitution, and inherently safer design, pp. 780-791

questions.stem: A valve requiring monthly service is placed above an operating line with no permanent access. What is the best design correction?
options: Require portable ladder use for every service
Issue a permit for each climb without changing the layout
Relocate the valve or provide permanent engineered access and isolation provisions
Extend the maintenance interval to once per year
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: PtD considers predictable maintenance and provides safe reach, access, isolation, and replacement space in the design.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Repeated portable access preserves fall and ergonomic exposure.
A permit controls work but does not correct poor maintainability.
Less frequent work does not make access safe when service is required.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 35, design stages and design safety reviews, pp. 785-795

questions.stem: Which valve design best demonstrates a fail-safe principle for loss of instrument air to a fuel line?
options: The valve remains at an unknown intermediate position
The valve opens fully to prevent pressure buildup
The operator must reach the valve before it changes state
The valve moves to the defined safe closed position on loss of air
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Fail-safe design selects a predictable state that minimizes the analyzed consequence when power or control energy is lost.
incorrectOptionExplanations: An indeterminate state does not provide a predictable safe response.
Opening a fuel line can increase fire or explosion risk unless a specific analysis proves otherwise.
A safety function should not rely solely on timely human intervention after utility loss.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 35, safety design reviews and hierarchy of controls, pp. 783-795

questions.stem: Which design review question best addresses end-of-life risk?
options: How will hazardous energy, residues, and materials be isolated and removed during decommissioning?
What color should the production dashboard use?
Which employee should receive the first operating award?
How many marketing brochures will be printed?
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Lifecycle design includes construction, operation, maintenance, modification, and decommissioning hazards.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Dashboard color is not an end-of-life hazard control question.
Recognition programs do not address decommissioning hazards.
Marketing volume is unrelated to safe dismantling and disposal.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 35, PtD stages including decommissioning, pp. 785-788

questions.stem: A multidisciplinary team needs a structured review of deviations such as more flow, less pressure, or reverse flow in a new process. Which method fits best?
options: A simple injury-rate trend
HAZOP
A payroll audit
A post-training satisfaction survey
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: HAZOP uses guide words and process parameters to identify credible deviations, causes, consequences, and safeguards.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Injury trends do not systematically test process deviations before operation.
Payroll auditing does not analyze process parameters and hazards.
A satisfaction survey evaluates reactions to training, not process design deviations.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 35, HAZOP and risk-assessment tools, pp. 791-793

questions.stem: A design team says safety requirements will be decided after equipment purchase. What is the main problem?
options: Purchased equipment can never be modified
Safety requirements are needed only for regulated chemicals
Safety criteria should be defined before selection so they can shape the design and procurement decision
Procurement cost is the only valid design criterion
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Explicit safety requirements early in design allow suppliers and reviewers to verify that hazards are eliminated or controlled by design.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Modification is possible, but late changes can be costly and limited.
PtD applies broadly to physical, chemical, ergonomic, and lifecycle hazards.
Cost must be balanced with function, risk, compliance, and lifecycle performance.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 35, design stages and safety design reviews, pp. 785-795

questions.stem: Two adjacent controls look identical but operate opposite equipment states. What design improvement is strongest?
options: Add a memo reminding operators to be careful
Discipline the next operator who selects the wrong control
Keep the controls identical to preserve symmetry
Differentiate and arrange the controls to match task logic, with clear feedback and error tolerance
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Human-centered design reduces error-likely conditions through compatible layout, differentiation, feedback, and recovery.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A memo is weaker than correcting a predictable interface-induced error.
Discipline does not correct the design condition that makes error likely.
Visual symmetry is not more important than reliable identification and operation.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapters 24 and 35, human factors and prevention through design, pp. 546-566 and 780-795

questions.stem: A machine guard was redesigned to improve access. What is needed before routine use?
options: Verify the changed design against hazards, requirements, interfaces, and foreseeable use
Accept it because production requested the change
Approve it based only on appearance
Wait for an incident to determine whether it is safe
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A design change should be reviewed and validated to confirm it does not introduce new hazards or defeat existing safeguards.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Business demand does not establish that hazards are controlled.
Appearance cannot verify strength, reach distances, interlocks, or maintenance access.
Post-incident learning is not an acceptable substitute for pre-use verification.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 35, design safety reviews and lifecycle assessment, pp. 785-795
